title: Title Strategy
description:
The commitment document. What we are building, for whom, on which platforms, by when — and, critically, the terms under which we stop.

Kill criteria are authored HERE, before any code exists and under a gate, not at prototype review. Criteria written at review time get written to justify the decision already made; criteria written in advance are a bet you can lose honestly. This is the single reason strategy survives as its own lifecycle state rather than folding into design.

one_liner.description: The game in one sentence a stranger would understand. If this is hard to write, the concept is not yet a concept.

why_this_opportunity.description: The argument, referencing claims. Not a restatement of the score.

platform_set.description: Platforms and their role. Roles are per-release policy at publication time, but the intended shape is set here so the design can be bound to the right constraints.

profile_version.description: Pinned so the design and the eventual build agree on which compliance rules applied.

session.description: Intent, not detail. The detailed session design belongs to game-design.

timebox_days.description: Concept to release candidate. The factory is built around 7-14 days; beyond ~21 this is a different kind of project.

mvp.description: What must exist for this to be a game at all.

out_of_scope.description: Named exclusions. Required and non-empty on purpose: a strategy that excludes nothing has not made a decision, and every attractive concept becomes an oversized project through additions nobody ever refused.

prototype_must_prove.description: The specific questions the prototype exists to answer. Without these the prototype becomes small production.

kill_criteria.description: The conditions under which we stop. Non-empty is enforced by gate G2. Each needs a rationale, because a criterion nobody can justify gets argued away at exactly the moment it matters.

sunset_floor.description: Sustained performance below this sunsets the title.

max_prototype_iterations.description: Bounded so ITERATE cannot become an infinite polish loop on the wrong game.

rollback_threshold.description: Defect severity at or above which a live release is rolled back.

concept.description: The concept the opportunity proposed, narrowed to the direction the title commits to. Still not a design: enough for design to start from without re-reading the opportunity.

gameplay_direction.description: The shape of play in a sentence or two: what a run or a level is, and what changes from one to the next.

control_scheme.description: One scheme. A title that needs two has two games' worth of onboarding.

replayability.description: Why a player starts another session. Replay should come from a system, not from more content.

production_scope.description: How big the commitment is, and what was done to keep it small. The timebox is the constraint; this is the evidence the scope fits it.

estimate_days.description: Estimated effort before the scope was fitted to the timebox. Above timebox_days means the scope was cut to fit; see scope_decisions.

reusable_systems.description: Systems taken from the template or an earlier title rather than built for this one.

scope_decisions.description: Each decision taken to keep the title small, in a sentence that says why.

platform_compatibility.description: Every candidate platform the opportunity named, checked against its pinned profile — including the ones left out of platform_set, so the reason for leaving them out is recorded.

sdk.description: What the platform SDK adapter must implement for this title. `none` for a platform with no SDK.

constraints.description: Binding profile requirements the design inherits.

origin.description: Carried over from the opportunity, or introduced by a decision taken here.

assumptions.description: What this strategy takes as true without having checked. Each names what would show it false, so the prototype and the first review know what to look at.
